items.stem: What is meant by "Unit of sale"?
items.answer: The basic unit in which a business sells its product or service, such as one cake, one kilogram or one hour.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The basic unit in which a business sells its product or service, such as one cake, one kilogram or one hour.

items.stem: Explain "Manufacturing business" with reference to the units of sale for different types of business.
items.answer: Manufacturing business: One unit of the product made, such as one chair or one cake.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: One unit of the product made, such as one chair or one cake.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The unit of sale is the same for all businesses.
Reason (R): A guest house sells room-nights while a bakery sells cakes.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: it differs by the type of business. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Kunal sells rice and pulses loose from sacks. What is the most suitable unit of sale?
items.answer: One kilogram
items.markingKey: (b) One kilogram. Loose goods are sold by weight.
options: One piece
One kilogram
One student per month
One hour of service

items.stem: Karthik runs a tuition centre, where the unit of sale is one student per month. The unit cost is ₹1,250. He wants a unit margin of 30% on cost. (a) What unit price should he charge? (b) What will be the total margin if 1,750 student-months are sold in a month? (c) Express the unit margin as a percentage of the unit price.

Singh Enterprises, a bakery in Agra, makes two products. Chocolate cake: unit price ₹110, material ₹35, labour ₹15, overhead ₹10 per unit, monthly sales 350 units. Loaf of bread: unit price ₹100, material ₹50, labour ₹20, overhead ₹5 per unit, monthly sales 800 units. (a) Calculate the unit cost and unit margin of each product. (b) Calculate the total monthly margin from each. (c) Which product earns more per unit and which earns more in total? Why do the two answers differ?
items.answer: (a) Chocolate cake: unit cost ₹60, unit margin ₹50; loaf of bread: unit cost ₹75, unit margin ₹25. (b) Chocolate cake: ₹50 × 350 = ₹17,500; loaf of bread: ₹25 × 800 = ₹20,000. (c) The chocolate cake earns more per unit, but the loaf of bread earns more in total, because total margin = unit margin × number of units and the loaf of bread sells many more units.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 1 mark. (a) Chocolate cake: unit cost ₹60, unit margin ₹50; loaf of bread: unit cost ₹75, unit margin ₹25. (b) Chocolate cake: ₹50 × 350 = ₹17,500; loaf of bread: ₹25 × 800 = ₹20,000. (c) The chocolate cake earns more per unit, but the loaf of bread earns more in total, because total margin = unit margin × number of units and the loaf of bread sells many more units.

items.stem: Kabir runs a tailoring shop in Nagpur. In a month he sold 1,500 shirts stitched at ₹600 each (unit of sale: one shirt stitched). The month's costs were: materials ₹4,94,000, wages ₹1,73,500, rent and other expenses ₹1,35,000. Calculate the unit cost and the unit margin.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for unit cost, 1 mark for unit margin. Total cost = ₹8,02,500; unit cost = ₹8,02,500 ÷ 1,500 = ₹535; unit margin = ₹600 − ₹535 = ₹65.

items.stem: Pooja runs a roadside eatery that serves thalis. What is the most suitable unit of sale? Justify your answer.
items.answer: One plate (meal). Meals are sold by the plate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying One plate (meal); 2 marks for the justification: Meals are sold by the plate.

items.stem: What is meant by "Contribution"?
items.answer: Selling price minus variable cost; the amount each unit contributes to fixed costs and profit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Selling price minus variable cost; the amount each unit contributes to fixed costs and profit.

items.stem: Explain "Helps in planning profit" with reference to the uses of break-even analysis for an entrepreneur.
items.answer: Helps in planning profit: Sales needed for a target profit can be found.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Sales needed for a target profit can be found.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about break-even analysis is NOT correct?
items.answer: A higher margin of safety means higher risk.
items.markingKey: (b) Incorrect statement: A higher margin of safety means higher risk.
options: At the break-even point, total revenue equals total cost.
A higher margin of safety means higher risk.
Rent is usually a fixed cost.
Margin of safety is actual sales minus break-even sales.

items.stem: Kabir makes candles in Surat. Fixed costs are ₹1,04,86,000 per year; selling price ₹1,890 and variable cost ₹1,355 per candle. Calculate the break-even point in units and in sales value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for BEP in units, 1 mark for BEP in rupees. Contribution per candle = ₹1,890 − ₹1,355 = ₹535. BEP = ₹1,04,86,000 ÷ ₹535 = 19,600 units; BEP sales = 19,600 × ₹1,890 = ₹3,70,44,000.

items.stem: Rao and Sons sells 250 notebooks a year at ₹1,575 each. Its fixed costs are ₹1,31,000 and the variable cost is ₹920 per notebook. Calculate (a) the break-even point in units, (b) the margin of safety in units and in rupees, and (c) the margin of safety as a percentage of actual sales.

Yash plans to make pickle jars. Fixed costs are ₹16,24,000 a year, the selling price is ₹380 and the variable cost is ₹235 per jar. How many units must he sell to (a) break even and (b) earn a profit of ₹11,09,250? (c) What will be the sales value in (b)?

Patel Industries, a small unit in Indore, makes school bags. Selling price ₹125 per bag; variable cost ₹110 per bag; fixed costs ₹1,44,000 a year. It expects to sell 16,850 units this year. (a) Calculate the contribution per unit and the break-even point in units. (b) Calculate the margin of safety in units and the expected profit. (c) If rent raises fixed costs by ₹29,550, find the new break-even point and comment.
items.answer: (a) Contribution = ₹125 − ₹110 = ₹15; BEP = ₹1,44,000 ÷ ₹15 = 9,600 units. (b) MoS = 16,850 − 9,600 = 7,250 units; profit = MoS × contribution = 7,250 × ₹15 = ₹1,08,750. (c) New BEP = ₹1,73,550 ÷ ₹15 = 11,570 units; expected sales still exceed it, so the firm stays profitable but its margin of safety falls to 5,280 units.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 1 mark. (a) Contribution = ₹125 − ₹110 = ₹15; BEP = ₹1,44,000 ÷ ₹15 = 9,600 units. (b) MoS = 16,850 − 9,600 = 7,250 units; profit = MoS × contribution = 7,250 × ₹15 = ₹1,08,750. (c) New BEP = ₹1,73,550 ÷ ₹15 = 11,570 units; expected sales still exceed it, so the firm stays profitable but its margin of safety falls to 5,280 units.

items.stem: Gupta Agencies, a small unit in Chandigarh, makes notebooks. Selling price ₹1,925 per notebook; variable cost ₹995 per notebook; fixed costs ₹1,58,56,500 a year. It expects to sell 31,050 units this year. (a) Calculate the contribution per unit and the break-even point in units. (b) Calculate the margin of safety in units and the expected profit. (c) If rent raises fixed costs by ₹31,15,500, find the new break-even point and comment.
items.answer: (a) Contribution = ₹1,925 − ₹995 = ₹930; BEP = ₹1,58,56,500 ÷ ₹930 = 17,050 units. (b) MoS = 31,050 − 17,050 = 14,000 units; profit = MoS × contribution = 14,000 × ₹930 = ₹1,30,20,000. (c) New BEP = ₹1,89,72,000 ÷ ₹930 = 20,400 units; expected sales still exceed it, so the firm stays profitable but its margin of safety falls to 10,650 units.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 1 mark. (a) Contribution = ₹1,925 − ₹995 = ₹930; BEP = ₹1,58,56,500 ÷ ₹930 = 17,050 units. items.stem: What is meant by "Working capital"?
items.answer: The funds needed for day-to-day operations, invested in current assets such as stock, debtors and cash.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The funds needed for day-to-day operations, invested in current assets such as stock, debtors and cash.

items.stem: Explain "Keep optimum inventory" with reference to the aims of working capital management.
items.answer: Keep optimum inventory: Neither shortage nor excess of stock.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the point and 1 mark for the explanation: Neither shortage nor excess of stock.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about working capital and inventory is NOT correct?
items.answer: Under FIFO, closing stock is valued at the oldest prices.
items.markingKey: (b) Incorrect statement: Under FIFO, closing stock is valued at the oldest prices.
options: Under FIFO, goods bought first are issued first.
Under FIFO, closing stock is valued at the oldest prices.

EOQ minimises the total of ordering and carrying costs.

Economic order quantity

items.stem: Riya runs a small factory that needs 2,16,000 kg of raw material a year. Ordering cost is ₹40 per order and carrying cost is ₹12 per kg per year. Calculate the economic order quantity and the number of orders to be placed in a year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for EOQ, 1 mark for the number of orders. EOQ = √(2 × 2,16,000 × 40 ÷ 12) = √14,40,000 = 1,200 kg. Number of orders = 2,16,000 ÷ 1,200 = 180.

items.stem: Nikhil runs Saxena Retail, a small manufacturing unit in Agra. (a) It uses 6,400 units of a component a year; ordering cost is ₹200 per order and carrying cost ₹4 per unit per year. Find the EOQ and the number of orders a year. (b) Its opening stock of finished goods was ₹1,85,000, closing stock ₹3,26,000 and cost of goods sold ₹10,22,000. Find the stock turnover ratio and the days stock is held (360-day year). (c) State what a low stock turnover would indicate.
items.answer: (a) EOQ = √(2 × 6,400 × 200 ÷ 4) = 800 units; orders = 6,400 ÷ 800 = 8. (b) Average inventory = ₹2,55,500; stock turnover = ₹10,22,000 ÷ ₹2,55,500 = 4 times; days = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 days. (c) A low ratio shows slow-moving or excess stock, which blocks working capital and raises carrying cost.

items.stem: Sethi Industries has shareholders' equity of ₹32,50,000 and long-term loans of ₹15,00,000. Its net profit after tax is ₹5,30,000. Calculate (a) return on equity and (b) return on investment (on total capital employed). (c) Why is ROE higher than ROI here?
items.answer: (a) ROE = ₹5,30,000 ÷ ₹32,50,000 × 100 = 16.31%. (b) ROI = ₹5,30,000 ÷ ₹47,50,000 × 100 = 11.16%. (c) Part of the capital is borrowed, so the profit is spread over a smaller equity base.

items.stem: Aryan runs Sethi Traders, a small manufacturing unit in Indore. (a) It uses 43,200 units of a component a year; ordering cost is ₹200 per order and carrying cost ₹12 per unit per year. Find the EOQ and the number of orders a year. (b) Its opening stock of finished goods was ₹2,81,000, closing stock ₹3,82,000 and cost of goods sold ₹33,15,000. Find the stock turnover ratio and the days stock is held (360-day year). (c) State what a low stock turnover would indicate.
items.answer: (a) EOQ = √(2 × 43,200 × 200 ÷ 12) = 1,200 units; orders = 43,200 ÷ 1,200 = 36. (b) Average inventory = ₹3,31,500; stock turnover = ₹33,15,000 ÷ ₹3,31,500 = 10 times; days = 360 ÷ 10 = 36 days. (c) A low ratio shows slow-moving or excess stock, which blocks working capital and raises carrying cost.

items.stem: Thakur and Sons, a bakery in Mumbai, makes two products. Loaf of bread: unit price ₹530, material ₹255, labour ₹50, overhead ₹35 per unit, monthly sales 1,100 units. Cupcake box: unit price ₹870, material ₹265, labour ₹145, overhead ₹95 per unit, monthly sales 350 units. (a) Calculate the unit cost and unit margin of each product. (b) Calculate the total monthly margin from each. (c) Which product earns more per unit and which earns more in total? Why do the two answers differ?
items.answer: (a) Loaf of bread: unit cost ₹340, unit margin ₹190; cupcake box: unit cost ₹505, unit margin ₹365. (b) Loaf of bread: ₹190 × 1,100 = ₹2,09,000; cupcake box: ₹365 × 350 = ₹1,27,750. (c) The cupcake box earns more per unit, but the loaf of bread earns more in total, because total margin = unit margin × number of units and the loaf of bread sells many more units.

(b) Loaf of bread: ₹190 × 1,100 = ₹2,09,000; cupcake box: ₹365 × 350 = ₹1,27,750. (c) The cupcake box earns more per unit, but the loaf of bread earns more in total, because total margin = unit margin × number of units and the loaf of bread sells many more units.
